title: Find out about unattended property laws
summary: Find out about the laws governing unattended property in public spaces across NSW.
intro: The NSW Government Public Spaces Unattended Property laws ensure public spaces (footpaths, streets, parks, bushland, and waterways) are safe and accessible for everyone.

more_info.text: Office of Local Government – Public Spaces Unattended Property Laws

external_links.text: Office of Local Government – Public Spaces Unattended Property Laws

faqs.q: What types of property are considered unattended?
faqs.a: Property considered unattended includes unregistered vehicles, personal recreation equipment, stray stock animals, share bikes, and shopping trolleys.

faqs.q: What are the penalties for unattended property?
faqs.a: Penalties can include on-the-spot fines, higher court penalties, rapid seizure action, and enforcement orders.

faqs.q: Where can I find more information about the laws?
faqs.a: You can view the Public Spaces Unattended Property laws at the NSW legislation website.
